body: Auto component makers supply OEMs (domestic and global) and the aftermarket. Profit depends on content per vehicle times OEM volumes, with commodity pass-through lagging by about a quarter. The aftermarket and replacement segment (tyres, batteries, filters) carries better margins and is less cyclical. Key metrics: revenue growth against underlying OEM production (outperformance shows content gains), order book and lifetime-value wins, EBITDA margin, RoCE, export share and geography, EV/powertrain-agnostic share, customer concentration, and working capital. Cycle drivers: domestic OEM cycles, global auto production (Europe and US trucks matter for forgings), tariffs (25% US tariff on Indian auto parts from 2025, Section 232), the EV transition shrinking ICE content, and the China+1 sourcing shift. Lead indicators: SIAM and Vahan, S&P Global Light Vehicle Production forecasts, US Class 8 truck orders (ACT Research), ACMA half-yearly data, EU registrations. Winners (Motherson via acquisitions-plus-integration, Uno Minda and Endurance via content-per-vehicle gains, Sona via EV-agnostic driveline) grew faster than OEM volumes, diversified customers and kept RoCE above 15%. Losers were single-customer suppliers, ICE-only powertrain parts, and debt-funded overseas acquisitions (Amtek Auto). Valuation: P/E 20–40x for growth and EV names, 12–20x for cyclical exporters. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 results were Sona revenue +35% (EV >50% of sales) with PAT +29%, and Sundram PAT +13%. New US contracts were in limbo due to tariffs (ACMA). Traps: order-book 'lifetime value', and EV hype multiples.

data.business_model: Content-per-vehicle x OEM volume; aftermarket replacement; exports to global OEMs/Tier-1s.
data.current_state_nov_2026: Sona Comstar Q2 FY27 PAT ₹223 cr (+29%), revenue +35%, EV >50% of sales. Sundram Fasteners Q2 FY27 PAT ~₹160–173 cr (+13–14%; sources differ). Indian auto-part exports to the US have faced a 25% tariff since 2025, and ACMA said new US supply contracts were in limbo.
data.cycle_drivers: OEM production cycles (domestic + global), commodity prices, FX, US/EU tariffs, EV transition, China+1.
traps: Lifetime order-win figures with unclear conversion
Exporters' FX gains read as operating improvement
data.valuation: P/E 12–20x (cyclical forgings/castings), 25–50x (EV, electronics, aftermarket franchises). Peaks: 2017–18, 2021, 2024. Troughs: FY20 (BS-VI + slowdown), Mar 2020.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Raw materials -> Tier-2/3 -> Tier-1 (system integrators) -> OEM; plus aftermarket distribution. Margins are best in proprietary systems, aftermarket and replacement tyres/batteries, and worst in build-to-print castings.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: rising content-per-vehicle, customer and geography diversification, powertrain-agnostic or EV products, disciplined M&A. Losers: single-OEM dependence, ICE-only parts, debt-heavy acquisitions, low-RoCE capex.

title: Sector playbook: Indian auto components
